change.1: OriginalMacDisplayBackend.frontKnown returns at once when presentUnknownAsBlack is set; its scan of the whole delivered rectangle (run in validateFront at both prepare and perform of every front Blt/fill) can only throw unknownPixel, which that flag rules out. Every host's runtime sets the flag (OriginalMacRuntimeStartup); unit tests construct the backend without it and still run the scan.
change.2: values/known storage accessors read once before each per-pixel loop (framebuffer, blt, drawText, front fill, front copy) instead of per pixel; nothing inside those loops records a deferred write or swaps storage.

profile after.note: frontCopy gone; memmove is now mostly copy-on-write of state records in the cycle's rollback copies (see probe)

macOS headless.after: 30.1 bodies/s, busy 16.4 s (now at the game's own rate)

review.verdict: OK: the skipped scan has no side effect other than draining deferred writes earlier, which is unobservable; no trap or throw possible in it with the flag set; flag immutable and set by every host; hoisted pointers cannot dangle or alias; first error thrown is unchanged for every input
notes: no unit test constructs the backend with presentUnknownAsBlack:true, so the early return is exercised by whole-runtime runs only
the frontCopy closure's rename is not a hoist; harmless since that path now runs only without the flag

copy-on-write probe (temporary, not comm.0x630e18 bytes (replay recording buffer): 1,659 copies, about one per gameplay cycle: ~21.5 GB of bytes plus definedness
copy-on-write probe (temporary, not comm.cause: rollback copies (var candidate = state ... state = candidate) share the arrays, so the first write per cycle duplicates each written record in full
